title: How Much Impact Does the President Have on Stocks? | Dimensional
gist: Dimensional pairs 100 years of S&P 500 growth-of-wealth data (January 1926 through December 2025) with presidential terms and macro series (real GDP growth, inflation, unemployment, federal surplus/deficit as % of GDP) to argue that US equities marched upward regardless of which administration held office. The piece is an argument against repositioning portfolios around election outcomes; the methodology notes reveal the data gaps (no unemployment before April 1929, no GDP before 1930, only one year for Trump's second term) that bound the comparison.

themes.theme: Elections as one input among many

insights.claim: Dimensional argues an election outcome is only one of many inputs to the market, so pre-election anticipation is a poor reason to alter equity positioning.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Fade election-driven rotation pitches; treat pre-election vol as a premium to sell rather than a signal to de-risk.
insights.quote: the outcome of an election is only one of many inputs to the market
insights.locator: The anticipation building up to elections

insights.claim: Across 100 years of US presidential terms, US equities show a consistent upward march regardless of which administration was in place, according to Dimensional's interactive exhibit of market and economic data.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: The base rate for staying invested through any administration is positive; party-of-the-president overlays have no demonstrated edge over a buy-and-hold benchmark.
insights.quote: shows a consistent upward march for US equities regardless of the administration in place

insights.claim: Dimensional frames the century-long equity record under alternating administrations as evidence for a long-term investment approach rather than tactical political timing.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: The house view behind Dimensional's product line is time-in-market over political timing; expect their fund flows and messaging to resist election-driven tactical shifts.
insights.quote: This is an important lesson on the benefits of a long-term investment approach.

insights.claim: The exhibit deliberately overlays political control data for the presidency, the House and the Senate onto the same timeline as equity and macro outcomes, implying no configuration of party control reliably maps to market results.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Divided-vs-unified-government trades are treated here as noise; the burden of proof sits with anyone claiming a durable congressional-control factor.
insights.locator: US Government Presidential and Congressional data

insights.claim: The study's full sample runs from January 1, 1926, through December 31, 2025, using the S&P 500 Index in US dollars as the proxy for stock returns.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Any conclusion drawn is a large-cap US-only result; it says nothing about small caps, value tilts, or non-US markets under different administrations.
insights.quote: Growth of wealth for the full sample from January 1, 1926, through December 31, 2025.

insights.claim: Per-term wealth growth is measured from each president's inauguration month up to but not including the successor's inauguration month, so returns are attributed by calendar tenure rather than by policy lag.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Attribution windows matter: returns driven by a predecessor's policy or by a handover-period shock get booked to the incoming president, which flatters or damns terms arbitrarily.
insights.quote: Growth of wealth for each presidential term starts on the inauguration month of each president up to but not including the inauguration month of a successor.
insights.locator: Growth of wealth for each presidential term

insights.claim: Calvin Coolidge's term in the exhibit starts on January 1, 1926 rather than at his inauguration because that is the inception date of the S&P 500 Index, truncating the earliest term in the sample.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: The first observation in the 100-year series is a partial term, so treat the earliest data points as structurally non-comparable.
insights.quote: Growth of wealth for Calvin Coolidge's term starts on January 1, 1926, based on the inception date of the S&P 500 Index.
insights.locator: Growth of wealth for Calvin Coolidge's term

insights.claim: Equity returns are paired with four macro series per term: federal surplus or deficit as a percentage of GDP, inflation and unemployment from the St. Louis Fed's FRED, and annual real GDP growth in constant 2012 dollars from the US Bureau of Economic Analysis.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
entities: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
insights.so_what: These are the variables Dimensional considers the relevant macro backdrop for equity outcomes; deficit-to-GDP sits alongside growth and inflation as a first-order term-level metric.
insights.locator: Federal surplus or deficit as a percentage of gross domestic product

themes.theme: Data gaps that bound the comparison

insights.claim: Unemployment data is not reported prior to April 1929 and GDP data is unavailable before 1930, so Herbert Hoover's real GDP growth is computed only from 1930 to 1932 and his federal budget from 1929 to 1932.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: The Depression-era term, the single worst equity stretch in the sample, has the thinnest macro coverage, which weakens any cross-term macro-to-returns inference.
insights.quote: Unemployment data not reported prior to April 1929.
insights.locator: For Herbert Hoover, the federal budget is calculated

insights.claim: For Donald Trump's second term, annual real GDP growth and the federal budget figure rest on a single year, calculated from January 1 through December 31, 2025.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: The most current administration's macro bars are a one-year snapshot, not a term average, so do not read them as comparable to completed four-year terms.
insights.quote: For Donald Trump's 2nd term, annual real GDP growth and federal budget are calculated from January 1 through December 31, 2025.

insights.claim: The growth-of-$1 chart is hypothetical and assumes reinvestment of income with no transaction costs or taxes, so the displayed compounding overstates what an investor could actually have realized.
insights.speaker: Dimensional Fund Advisors
insights.so_what: Discount the headline wealth multiple for frictions before using it as a benchmark for real after-tax portfolio outcomes.
insights.quote: Data presented in the growth of $1 chart is hypothetical and assume reinvestment of income and no transaction costs or taxes.
insights.locator: Data presented in the growth of $1 chart
